metadata.description: Code examples with bugs for training bug detection and fixing skills

examples.title: SQL Injection Vulnerability
examples.bug_explanation: Direct string concatenation in SQL queries allows SQL injection attacks. An attacker could input: admin' OR '1'='1 to bypass authentication.
examples.fix_explanation: Use parameterized queries where the database driver handles escaping. This prevents injection by treating user input as data, not executable code.

test_cases.buggy_behavior: Returns all users or first user (security breach)
test_cases.fixed_behavior: Returns None (no user with that exact username)

examples.title: Incorrect Array Comparison
examples.bug_explanation: In JavaScript, arrays are objects and == compares references, not contents. This will always return false for different array instances, even with identical contents.
examples.fix_explanation: Properly compare array contents by checking length first, then using every() to compare each element.

examples.title: Mutable Default Argument
examples.bug_explanation: Default arguments are evaluated once at function definition, not each call. The same list is reused across calls, causing unexpected state sharing.
examples.fix_explanation: Use None as default and create a new list inside the function. This ensures each call gets a fresh list when no argument is provided.

examples.title: Race Condition in Counter
examples.bug_explanation: count++ is not atomic (read-modify-write). Multiple threads can read the same value, increment it, and write back, losing increments.
examples.fix_explanation: Use AtomicInteger which provides atomic operations. Alternatively, synchronize the increment method, but AtomicInteger is more performant.
examples.test_scenario: 10 threads each incrementing 1000 times. Expected: 10000. Buggy version: ~9500-9900 (lost updates). Fixed version: 10000.

examples.title: Inefficient List Membership Testing
examples.bug_explanation: 'in' operation on lists is O(n). For large lists, this becomes O(n²) overall, causing severe performance degradation.
examples.fix_explanation: Use a set for O(1) average-case membership testing, reducing overall complexity to O(n).

examples.title: Closure in Loop
examples.bug_explanation: var is function-scoped, not block-scoped. All closures reference the same 'i' variable, which equals 5 after the loop completes.
examples.fix_explanation: Use 'let' which is block-scoped - each iteration gets its own 'i'. Alternative: use IIFE to capture value.

examples.title: Command Injection
examples.bug_explanation: User input directly in shell command allows injection. Input like '8.8.8.8; rm -rf /' could execute arbitrary commands.
examples.fixed_code:
import subprocess

def ping_host(hostname):
    # Validate hostname format
    import re
    if not re.match(r'^[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+$', hostname):
        raise ValueError('Invalid hostname')
    
    # Use list form (no shell interpretation)
    subprocess.run(['ping', '-c', '4', hostname], check=True, capture_output=True)
examples.fix_explanation: 1) Validate input format, 2) Use subprocess with list arguments (no shell), preventing injection. Each argument is passed separately, not interpreted by shell.
examples.security_impact: Critical - can lead to complete system compromise

examples.title: Goroutine Leak
examples.bug_explanation: Goroutines are blocked writing to channel after first read. If items has 100 elements, 99 goroutines leak, never terminating.
examples.better_fix: Use sync.WaitGroup or context for proper goroutine lifecycle management, or use buffered channel and read all results.
examples.impact: Memory leak, goroutine exhaustion in long-running applications

examples.title: Floating Point Comparison
examples.bug_explanation: Floating point arithmetic is imprecise due to binary representation. 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004 in JavaScript.
examples.fix_explanation: Compare the absolute difference against a small epsilon value. Choose epsilon based on required precision.
examples.real_world_impact: Financial calculations, scientific computing, game physics - anywhere precision matters

examples.title: Shallow Copy Mutation
examples.buggy_code:
def process_data(data):
    # Attempt to create independent copy
    new_data = data
    new_data['processed'] = True
    return new_data

original = {'value': 42}
result = process_data(original)
print(original)  # {'value': 42, 'processed': True} - MUTATED!
examples.bug_explanation: Assignment creates reference, not copy. Both variables point to same object, so modifications affect original.
examples.fixed_code:
import copy

def process_data(data):
    new_data = copy.deepcopy(data)  # For nested structures
    # Or for simple dicts: new_data = data.copy() or dict(data)
    new_data['processed'] = True
    return new_data

original = {'value': 42}
result = process_data(original)
print(original)  # {'value': 42} - unchanged
examples.fix_explanation: Use copy.deepcopy() for nested structures or dict.copy() for shallow dictionaries. Understand copy vs deepcopy semantics.
examples.when_this_matters: Data pipelines, function purity, preventing side effects

code_smell_detection.title: Long Method
code_smell_detection.code:
def process_order(order_data):
    # Validate customer (10 lines)
    # Check inventory (15 lines)
    # Calculate pricing (20 lines)
    # Apply discounts (12 lines)
    # Process payment (18 lines)
    # Update inventory (10 lines)
    # Send notifications (8 lines)
    # Generate invoice (15 lines)
    # Update analytics (10 lines)
    # Return response (5 lines)
    pass  # 123 lines total
code_smell_detection.refactored_approach:
def process_order(order_data):
    customer = validate_customer(order_data)
    inventory_check(order_data.items)
    pricing = calculate_pricing(order_data)
    final_price = apply_discounts(pricing, customer)
    payment = process_payment(final_price, customer)
    update_inventory(order_data.items)
    send_notifications(customer, order_data)
    invoice = generate_invoice(order_data, final_price)
    update_analytics(order_data)
    return create_response(invoice, payment)
